name: Multi-Agent Research System
pitch: Compares three ways LLM agents coordinate to research a topic and write reports.
description: You give it a research topic. A team of AI agents searches the web, pulls out key facts, analyzes them and writes a structured report. The same job runs three ways (fixed pipeline, shared blackboard memory, critic feedback loop), and a Streamlit dashboard scores and compares the results.

hardestProblem: Making a pipeline written for one paid API run reliably on free and local models: a provider switch (Anthropic, Groq, Ollama) behind the interface the agents already used, a parser fix for Markdown-bolded output that silently dropped every source, output headroom for a reasoning model whose hidden tokens truncated JSON, and rate-limit handling for Groq's per-minute and per-day quotas.

highlights: Built a multi-agent research pipeline in Python with five specialized LLM agents (query generation, search, extraction, analysis, report) plus a critic, run under three coordination strategies for side-by-side comparison.
Implemented a critic feedback loop that scores drafts against a 7.5/10 threshold and sends specific feedback back for up to 3 revisions each of the analysis and the report.

Built an LLM-as-judge evaluation that scores each report on quality, factual accuracy and hallucination rate, combines them into a weighted composite (35/35/30), and reports a winner per metric in a Streamlit + Plotly dashboard.

Added a provider layer so the same agents run on Anthropic Claude, Groq or a local Ollama model from one .env setting, letting the project run with no paid API key (full local run in 7 min 17 s on an RTX 3050 6 GB).

Fixed reliability problems that showed up on new models: a parser that silently dropped Markdown-formatted results, JSON truncated by a reasoning model's hidden tokens, and free-tier rate limits handled with retries and a clear daily-quota error.
Integrated Tavily web search with URL de-duplication and a clearly labelled LLM-simulated fallback; a full 3-strategy run with real search finished in 5 min 41 s.
